main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Physics
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Physics
learning_activity_name: Explain the fundamental principles of measurement (dimensional analysis, precision, accuracy and uncertainties)
sla_assessment_criteria: Fundamental principles of measurements are clearly explained.
sla_teaching_aids: Metre rule|Vernier calipers|Voltmeters|Ammeters|Micrometer screw gauge|Weighing scales/ balances|Timers or stopwatches|Protractor|Oscilloscope
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Every physical measurement has a unit, a dimension and an uncertainty, and advanced physics uses these ideas to check equations and judge the quality of results.
sla_notes_details: Dimensional analysis expresses a quantity in terms of the base dimensions M (mass), L (length), T (time), I (current) and temperature. It is used to check the homogeneity of equations, to derive relations between quantities and to convert units, although it cannot fix dimensionless constants. Precision describes how closely repeated readings agree (small scatter), while accuracy describes how close a reading is to the true value. Random errors are reduced by repeating and averaging, whereas systematic errors (zero error, faulty calibration) shift all readings one way. Uncertainty is given as absolute, fractional or percentage uncertainty. For sums and differences absolute uncertainties add; for products and quotients fractional uncertainties add; for a power x^n the fractional uncertainty is multiplied by n.
sla_notes_illustrations: Check the equation v = u + at: dimensions of v are LT^-1, of u LT^-1 and of at (LT^-2)(T) = LT^-1, so the equation is homogeneous. A length is measured as 20.0 ± 0.1 cm and a width as 5.0 ± 0.1 cm; the area is 100 cm² with percentage uncertainty 0.5% + 2.0% = 2.5%, i.e. 100 ± 3 cm².
sla_notes_daily_life: Builders, tailors, pharmacists and laboratory technicians all rely on correct units and known uncertainty so that materials fit, doses are safe and results can be trusted.
sla_exercise: Write the dimensions of force.::MLT^-2, since force = mass x acceleration.||A radius is measured as 4.0 ± 0.1 cm. Find the percentage uncertainty in the area of the circle (A = πr²).::Percentage uncertainty in r = 2.5%, so in r² it is 2 x 2.5% = 5%.||Distinguish precision from accuracy.::Precision is the closeness of repeated readings to each other; accuracy is the closeness of a reading to the true value.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Physics
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Physics
learning_activity_name: Describe the basic tenets of mechanics and two dimensional motion (projectile motion, circular motion, rotation, gravitation and fluid mechanics)
sla_assessment_criteria: Concepts and principles related to mechanics are correctly described.
sla_teaching_aids: Balls|Conical pendulum|Banked road|Water in bucket|Telescope|Solid object|Earth globe|Armfield F1-15|Bernoulli’s apparatus test equipment|Calipers or metre rules|Jug|F1-10 hydraulic bench|Stopwatch|Electric motor
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Mechanics explains how bodies move under forces, from a thrown ball to a planet, and at advanced level it includes motion in two dimensions, rotation, gravitation and fluids.
sla_notes_details: Projectile motion is the combination of uniform horizontal velocity and vertical motion under g: range R = u² sin2θ / g, maximum height H = u² sin²θ / 2g and time of flight T = 2u sinθ / g. In uniform circular motion the centripetal acceleration is a = v²/r = ω²r and the force is F = mv²/r directed to the centre; it explains banked roads and the conical pendulum. Rotation uses torque τ = Iα, angular momentum L = Iω and rotational kinetic energy ½Iω², with conservation of angular momentum when no external torque acts. Gravitation follows F = GMm/r², with field strength g = GM/r², potential V = -GM/r and orbital speed v = √(GM/r); Kepler's third law states T² ∝ r³. In fluids, pressure P = ρgh, the equation of continuity A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ and Bernoulli's principle P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant describe flow, while viscosity gives Stokes' law F = 6πηrv.
sla_notes_illustrations: A ball is kicked at 20 m/s at 30° above the ground (g = 10 m/s²). Range = 400 x sin60° / 10 = 34.6 m and maximum height = 400 x 0.25 / 20 = 5 m. A satellite at radius r = 7.0 x 10⁶ m around Earth (GM = 4.0 x 10¹⁴) moves at √(4.0 x 10¹⁴ / 7.0 x 10⁶) ≈ 7.6 km/s.
sla_notes_daily_life: Sports such as football and javelin, banked curves on highways, spinning washing machines, satellites for television and telephone, and the lift of an aeroplane wing all depend on these principles.
sla_exercise: State the two components of projectile motion.::Uniform velocity in the horizontal direction and uniformly accelerated motion (acceleration g) in the vertical direction.||Calculate the centripetal force on a 2 kg mass moving at 3 m/s in a circle of radius 1.5 m.::F = mv²/r = 2 x 9 / 1.5 = 12 N.||State Bernoulli's principle.::For steady flow of an ideal fluid, where the speed is high the pressure is low, because P + ½ρv² + ρgh remains constant along a streamline.

specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Physics
learning_activity_name: Describe the fundamental concepts, principles and theories underlying the thermal properties of materials (heat transfer, kinetic theory of solids, liquids and gases, thermodynamics and thermal radiation)
sla_assessment_criteria: Concepts, principles and theories underlying the thermal properties of materials are correctly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Thermal physics explains how heat moves, how gases behave and how energy is converted, using both the kinetic model and the laws of thermodynamics.
sla_notes_details: Heat is transferred by conduction, convection and radiation; conduction obeys Q/t = kA(θ₁ - θ₂)/L, and a black body radiates according to Stefan's law P = σAT⁴. The kinetic theory of gases gives PV = ⅓Nm<c²> and, with the ideal-gas law PV = nRT, the mean kinetic energy per molecule ½m<c²> = 3kT/2, so temperature measures the average molecular energy. Specific heat capacity is c = Q/mΔθ and the latent heat is Q = mL. The first law of thermodynamics is ΔU = Q - W, where W = PΔV for expansion; in an isothermal change PV is constant, in an adiabatic change PV^γ is constant. The second law states that heat does not flow spontaneously from a cold body to a hot body and that heat engines have efficiency η = 1 - T_c/T_h at best.
sla_notes_illustrations: A cylinder of gas of 2.0 mol at 300 K has pressure P = nRT/V = 2 x 8.31 x 300 / 0.05 = 1.0 x 10⁵ Pa for V = 0.05 m³. If 500 J of heat is supplied to a gas which does 200 J of work, its internal energy rises by 300 J.
sla_notes_daily_life: Refrigerators, car engines, thermos flasks, solar cookers, cooking pots with wooden handles and the cooling of the body by sweating all apply thermal physics.
sla_exercise: State the first law of thermodynamics.::The heat supplied to a system equals the increase in its internal energy plus the work done by the system: Q = ΔU + W.||Find the mean kinetic energy of a gas molecule at 27 °C (k = 1.38 x 10⁻²³ J/K).::E = 3kT/2 = 1.5 x 1.38 x 10⁻²³ x 300 = 6.2 x 10⁻²¹ J.||Name the three modes of heat transfer.::Conduction, convection and radiation.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Physics
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Physics
learning_activity_name: Explore the basic tenets of vibrations and waves (simple harmonic motion, and wave propagation {interference, diffraction and polarization})
sla_method: Group discussion and Interactive simulation and virtual labs
sla_assessment_criteria: Concepts, theories and principles related to vibrations and waves are correctly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Vibrations and waves describe repeating motion and the way energy travels without the transport of matter.
sla_notes_details: In simple harmonic motion the acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed to the equilibrium point: a = -ω²x, with x = A sin(ωt), period T = 2π/ω, and for a spring T = 2π√(m/k) and for a simple pendulum T = 2π√(L/g). Energy exchanges between kinetic and potential forms with total energy ½kA². Damping reduces amplitude and resonance occurs when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency. A progressive wave has v = fλ; stationary waves form from superposition of two waves of the same frequency travelling in opposite directions and have nodes and antinodes. Interference requires coherent sources: constructive when the path difference is nλ and destructive when it is (n + ½)λ. Young's double slit gives fringe separation x = λD/a, a diffraction grating gives d sinθ = nλ, and polarization shows that light is a transverse wave.
sla_notes_illustrations: A pendulum of length 1.0 m on Earth (g = 9.8 m/s²) has period 2π√(1/9.8) = 2.0 s. In a Young's experiment with λ = 600 nm, D = 2.0 m and slit separation a = 0.60 mm, the fringe separation is 600 x 10⁻⁹ x 2.0 / 0.60 x 10⁻³ = 2.0 mm.
sla_notes_daily_life: Musical instruments, vibration of bridges and buildings during earthquakes, radio tuning, noise-cancelling headphones, polarizing sunglasses and the colours on a compact disc all involve vibrations and waves.
sla_exercise: State the condition for simple harmonic motion.::The acceleration is proportional to the displacement from the equilibrium position and is always directed towards it.||Find the frequency of a spring-mass system with k = 200 N/m and m = 0.5 kg.::f = (1/2π)√(k/m) = (1/2π)√400 = 20/2π ≈ 3.2 Hz.||What path difference gives destructive interference of two coherent waves of wavelength λ?::An odd number of half wavelengths, (n + ½)λ.

learning_activity_name: Explain the concept, theories and principles of electrostatics (electric field, electric potential and capacitance)
sla_assessment_criteria: Concept, theories and principles of electrostatics are correctly explained.
sla_teaching_aids: Plastic rods|Glass rods|Voltmeter|Capacitance meter|Multimeter|Potentiometer|Metre bridge|Electroscope|Metal plate|Battery
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Electrostatics studies charges at rest, the forces between them and the energy stored in electric fields.
sla_notes_details: Coulomb's law gives F = Q₁Q₂ / 4πε₀r². Electric field strength E = F/q; for a point charge E = Q / 4πε₀r² and between parallel plates E = V/d. Electric potential at a point V = Q / 4πε₀r is the work per unit charge to bring a positive charge from infinity, and E = -dV/dr. Equipotential surfaces are always perpendicular to field lines. Capacitance C = Q/V; for parallel plates C = ε₀εᵣA/d. Capacitors in parallel add (C = C₁ + C₂) while in series 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂. The energy stored is W = ½QV = ½CV² = Q²/2C. Charging and discharging through a resistor follow exponential laws with time constant τ = RC, for example Q = Q₀e^(-t/RC) during discharge.
sla_notes_illustrations: Two plates of area 0.02 m² are separated by 1.0 mm of air: C = 8.85 x 10⁻¹² x 0.02 / 1.0 x 10⁻³ = 1.8 x 10⁻¹⁰ F. A 100 µF capacitor charged to 12 V stores ½ x 100 x 10⁻⁶ x 144 = 7.2 mJ, and with R = 10 kΩ the time constant is 1 s.
sla_notes_daily_life: Lightning conductors, photocopiers, electrostatic spray painting, camera flash units, touch screens and the smoothing of power supplies in phone chargers use electrostatic principles.
sla_exercise: Define capacitance.::Capacitance is the charge stored per unit potential difference, C = Q/V, measured in farads.||Two 6 µF capacitors are connected in series. Find the total capacitance.::1/C = 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3, so C = 3 µF.||What is the time constant of a circuit with R = 2 kΩ and C = 50 µF?::τ = RC = 2000 x 50 x 10⁻⁶ = 0.1 s.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Physics
specific_competence_name: Use various instruments to carry out measurements in Physics
learning_activity_name: Use various instruments to carry out experiments in mechanics, vibrations and waves, thermal properties of materials and electrostatics
sla_assessment_criteria: Various measuring instruments are applied accordingly in mechanics, vibrations and waves, thermal properties of materials and electrostatics.
sla_teaching_aids: Flow-tube|Thermometers|Vernier calipers|Pendulum|Inclined planes|Ripple tanks|Tuning fork|Spectrometer|Thermocouple|CRT (Cathode Ray Tube) sonometer|Stopwatch|Retort stand|Steel balls of varying diameters
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Correct use of instruments is the basis of reliable experiments in mechanics, waves, thermal physics and electrostatics.
sla_notes_details: Students learn to select an instrument according to the range and the smallest scale division needed. The vernier caliper reads to 0.1 mm or 0.05 mm and the micrometer screw gauge to 0.01 mm after correcting for zero error. Stopwatches and light gates measure time, the thermocouple and thermometers measure temperature, the oscilloscope displays voltage against time so that amplitude and frequency can be found (f = 1/T from the time-base), and the capacitance meter and multimeter measure electrical quantities. Good practice includes checking zero errors, taking repeated readings, avoiding parallax, working in a tabulated form and recording units and uncertainties. Instruments are connected to the correct range to avoid damage, for example an ammeter always in series and a voltmeter in parallel.
sla_notes_illustrations: To find the acceleration of a ball on an inclined plane, time it over a measured distance using a stopwatch, repeat five times and use s = ½at². With a micrometer of zero error +0.02 mm reading 1.35 mm for a wire diameter, the true diameter is 1.33 mm.
sla_notes_daily_life: Technicians measure engine parts with calipers, nurses use thermometers, electricians use multimeters and mechanics use gauges, so skill with instruments carries over to many careers.
sla_exercise: A micrometer has a zero error of +0.03 mm and reads 2.47 mm. What is the correct reading?::2.47 - 0.03 = 2.44 mm.||How is an oscilloscope used to find the frequency of a signal?::Measure the period T from the horizontal divisions multiplied by the time-base setting, then f = 1/T.||Why is an ammeter connected in series?::It must carry the same current as the component being measured, and it has a very small resistance so that it does not change that current.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Physics
specific_competence_name: Use various instruments to carry out measurements in Physics
learning_activity_name: Analyse the precision and accuracy of measurements
sla_assessment_criteria: Precision and accuracy of measurements is correctly processed.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Analysing measurement data shows how much confidence can be placed in a result and how experiments can be improved.
sla_notes_details: Precision is judged from the spread of repeated readings, expressed as the mean and standard deviation or the range/2, while accuracy is judged by comparing the mean with the accepted value using percentage difference. Systematic errors are found by plotting a graph and seeing a non-zero intercept where zero is expected; random errors appear as scatter about the best-fit line. The gradient uncertainty is estimated from the steepest and least steep acceptable lines. Improvements include using instruments with finer scale divisions, increasing the number of readings, measuring a large quantity (for example the time for 20 oscillations), controlling variables and calibrating instruments. Results are presented with the correct significant figures matching the uncertainty.
sla_notes_illustrations: Five timings of 20 oscillations of a pendulum give 41.2, 41.5, 41.3, 41.4 and 41.1 s. The mean is 41.3 s and the range/2 is 0.2 s, so T = 2.065 ± 0.010 s, a percentage uncertainty of about 0.5%.
sla_notes_daily_life: Bakers weighing ingredients, farmers calibrating scales at the market and factories controlling product size all need measurements that are both precise and accurate.
sla_exercise: Explain how a set of readings can be precise but not accurate.::The readings are close to each other, but a systematic error such as a zero error shifts all of them away from the true value.||Readings of 10.2, 10.4 and 10.3 cm are taken. Find the mean and the uncertainty using half the range.::Mean = 10.3 cm; half the range = 0.1 cm, so 10.3 ± 0.1 cm.||Give one way of reducing the percentage uncertainty in a period measurement.::Time many oscillations, for example 20, and divide by 20.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Physics
specific_competence_name: Analyse the efficacy of different techniques and instruments in physical measurements
learning_activity_name: Analyse the strengths and weaknesses of various instruments and techniques used in mechanics, vibrations and waves, thermal properties of materials and electrostatics
sla_name: Strengths and weaknesses of instruments and techniques
sla_assessment_criteria: Strengths and weaknesses of various techniques and instruments used in physical measurements are correctly analysed.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: No instrument or technique is perfect, so physicists compare methods and select the one that gives the best result for the task.
sla_notes_details: A vernier caliper is quick and versatile but less sensitive than a micrometer; a stopwatch depends on human reaction time (about 0.2 s) while a light gate with a datalogger is far more precise but costs more and needs a computer. Thermocouples respond quickly and cover a wide range but need calibration, whereas liquid-in-glass thermometers are cheap but slow and fragile. The oscilloscope shows rapidly changing signals but has a limited reading accuracy. Techniques such as the resonance-tube method for the speed of sound or the ripple tank for waves also have limits: end corrections, damping and parallax. Analysis therefore considers sensitivity, range, response time, cost, safety and the availability of materials, and proposes improvements or alternatives.
sla_notes_illustrations: To measure the speed of sound, the resonance tube gives v = 4f(L + 0.3d), which corrects for end effect, whereas timing an echo by stopwatch over 100 m has a large error because reaction time is comparable to the travel time of about 0.6 s.
sla_notes_daily_life: Choosing between a cheap thermometer and a digital probe, or between a tape measure and a laser distance meter, involves the same balance of cost, speed and accuracy in daily work.
sla_exercise: State one weakness of timing with a stopwatch.::Human reaction time introduces a systematic error of about 0.2 s.||Why is a micrometer preferred to a metre rule for measuring the thickness of wire?::It has a finer scale division (0.01 mm) so the percentage uncertainty is much smaller.||Name one advantage of a datalogger with light gates.::It measures short time intervals automatically and with high precision without reaction-time error.

main_competence_name: Conduct experiments in Physics
specific_competence_name: Carry out experiments in Physics
learning_activity_name: Design and carry out scientific experiments related to mechanics, vibrations and waves, thermal properties of materials and electrostatics
sla_name: Designing and carrying out physics experiments
sla_assessment_criteria: Experiments are designed and carried out according to underlying procedures.
sla_teaching_aids: Calorimeters|Thermometers|Source of heat|Micrometer screw gauge|Slotted weights|Metre rule|Ripple tank|Resonance tube|Vernier calipers
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A well-designed experiment tests a clear hypothesis by changing one variable, measuring another and controlling everything else.
sla_notes_details: The design begins with a question, identifies the independent, dependent and control variables, lists apparatus, describes the procedure step by step, and states the safety precautions and expected treatment of data. Linearisation turns a relationship into y = mx + c so that a straight-line graph gives the required constant, for example plotting T² against L for a pendulum to obtain g = 4π²/gradient. Typical experiments are the specific heat capacity of a metal by electrical method, the speed of sound by resonance, the acceleration due to gravity by a pendulum or free fall, the surface tension of a liquid and the charging and discharging of a capacitor. Results are recorded in tables, graphed, analysed for uncertainty and compared with theory in a conclusion and evaluation.
sla_notes_illustrations: In the pendulum experiment, L = 0.40, 0.60, 0.80, 1.00 m gives T² = 1.61, 2.42, 3.22, 4.03 s². The gradient is 4.03 s²/m, so g = 4π²/4.03 = 9.8 m/s².
sla_notes_daily_life: Testing which cooking oil heats fastest, checking a fertilizer trial or comparing insulating materials for a cold box use the same planning of variables and data analysis.
sla_exercise: Identify the independent and dependent variables in an experiment on how the period of a pendulum depends on its length.::The length is the independent variable and the period is the dependent variable.||What should be plotted to obtain g from a pendulum experiment?::Plot T² against L; the gradient is 4π²/g.||List two safety precautions when heating water electrically in a calorimeter.::Keep water away from electrical connections and switch off before touching hot equipment; use insulated leads and do not overfill.

learning_activity_name: Use ICT tools to analyse and present data (Ms Excel, PSPP, R, MATLAB, Python and Origin)
sla_name: Using ICT tools to analyse and present physics data
sla_assessment_criteria: Data are analysed and presented using ICT tools.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Software helps physicists process large sets of data quickly, draw graphs and present results clearly.
sla_notes_details: Spreadsheets such as MS Excel are used to enter data, calculate means and uncertainties with formulae, plot scatter graphs, add trendlines and read gradients and intercepts. Statistical packages such as PSPP and R give descriptive statistics, correlation and regression. MATLAB and Python (with libraries such as NumPy and Matplotlib) handle numerical modelling, curve fitting and plotting, and Origin is used for scientific graphs with error bars and fitting. The steps are to import clean data, check for outliers, choose a suitable graph type, label axes with quantities and units, fit a model, record the goodness of fit and export figures for a report.
sla_notes_illustrations: Entering the pendulum data in Excel with L in column A and T² in column B, inserting a scatter chart and a linear trendline gives y = 4.03x + 0.00 with R² = 0.999, from which g is found as 4π²/4.03. In Python, numpy.polyfit(L, T2, 1) returns the same gradient.
sla_notes_daily_life: Weather services, hospitals and telecommunication companies analyse data with the same tools to draw graphs, predict trends and share results.
sla_exercise: Name two ICT tools that can be used to plot and fit a graph.::Any two of MS Excel, Origin, MATLAB, Python (Matplotlib) or R.||What does a trendline in a spreadsheet give?::The best-fit line equation, including gradient and intercept, and possibly the R² value.||Why should axes of a graph be labelled with quantity and unit?::So that the reader knows what is plotted and can interpret the gradient and values correctly.

learning_activity_name: Use various methods to disseminate scientific results in Physics (reports, journal articles and case studies)
sla_assessment_criteria: Various methods are used to disseminate scientific results.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Science is complete only when results are communicated so that others can understand, check and use them.
sla_notes_details: Results are shared through laboratory reports, journal articles, case studies, posters and oral presentations. A report has a title, abstract, introduction and aim, theory, method, results in tables and graphs, analysis with uncertainties, discussion and conclusion, and references. A journal article is peer reviewed and follows a stricter format; a case study describes the application of physics to a specific real situation. The language is objective and in the past tense, sources are acknowledged using a reference style such as APA to avoid plagiarism, and data are presented honestly without changing values. Presenting orally requires clear slides, logical order and answering questions.
sla_notes_illustrations: After the specific heat experiment, a student writes a one-page abstract: c of copper was found to be 390 ± 20 J/kg K compared with the accepted 385 J/kg K, so the result agrees within uncertainty. The report includes a graph of temperature against time with error bars.
sla_notes_daily_life: Engineers writing reports for clients, health workers presenting findings to a ministry and students presenting a science fair exhibit all use the same structure of communicating results.
sla_exercise: List the main sections of a laboratory report.::Title, abstract, introduction and aim, theory, method, results, analysis, discussion, conclusion and references.||Why must the sources used in a report be acknowledged?::To give credit to the authors and avoid plagiarism, and to allow readers to check the information.||What is a case study in physics?::A detailed study of how physics principles apply to a specific real situation, such as the design of a solar water heater.

main_competence_name: Conduct a project in Physics
specific_competence_name: Conduct a project in Physics
learning_activity_name: Design and carry out a research project in Physics
sla_assessment_criteria: Research project has been designed and carried out by considering scientific procedures.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A research project lets students investigate a real problem in their environment using the scientific method over several months.
sla_notes_details: The process starts with identifying a problem, reviewing literature, stating objectives and hypotheses, and choosing methods, materials and a timetable. Ideas may include a solar dryer for crops, a low-cost water level indicator, a wind-powered pump, the thermal properties of local building materials, or a study of the intensity of sunlight in a region. Students prepare a proposal, build a prototype or plan a field survey, collect data with appropriate instruments, keep a logbook, analyse and discuss results and later write a report. Ethical practice, safety, sharing of tasks in groups and budgeting are part of the project.
sla_notes_illustrations: A group proposes to compare the heating rate of water in a black and in a white container under sunlight. They define variables, measure temperature every 5 minutes with thermometers for 60 minutes, plot graphs and conclude that the black container absorbs radiation faster, which is consistent with radiation theory.
sla_notes_daily_life: Solutions such as solar cookers, improved cooking stoves, charging devices and water pumps for farms often begin as school or community physics projects.
sla_exercise: State the first step in the design of a research project.::Identify a problem or question to investigate.||Why is a hypothesis stated before collecting data?::It gives a testable prediction that guides the choice of variables, methods and analysis.||Suggest one project topic in physics using local materials.::A solar dryer for fruits, or comparing the thermal insulation of different roofing materials.

learning_activity_name: Explain the principles, theories and concepts of current electricity (direct and alternating current and electrical networks)
sla_assessment_criteria: Principles, theories and concepts of current electricity are clearly explained.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Current electricity deals with the steady flow of charge in circuits, including direct and alternating current and the analysis of networks.
sla_notes_details: Current I = ΔQ/Δt, potential difference V = W/Q and resistance R = V/I (Ohm's law for ohmic conductors). Resistivity gives R = ρL/A. For a cell of e.m.f. E and internal resistance r, V = E - Ir. Kirchhoff's first law (conservation of charge) states that the sum of currents into a junction is zero, and the second law (conservation of energy) states that the sum of e.m.f.s equals the sum of potential drops around a loop; they are used to solve networks. The Wheatstone bridge is balanced when P/Q = R/S, and the potentiometer compares e.m.f.s and measures internal resistance without drawing current at balance. Alternating current i = I₀ sin ωt has r.m.s. value I₀/√2; in series RLC circuits the impedance is Z = √(R² + (X_L - X_C)²) with X_L = ωL and X_C = 1/ωC, and resonance occurs at f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)). Power in a.c. is P = I_rms V_rms cosφ.
sla_notes_illustrations: A cell of e.m.f. 6.0 V and internal resistance 1.0 Ω is connected to a 5.0 Ω resistor: I = 6/(5 + 1) = 1.0 A and terminal voltage = 5.0 V. For an L = 0.10 H and C = 10 µF circuit, f₀ = 1/(2π√(10⁻⁶)) ≈ 160 Hz.
sla_notes_daily_life: Household wiring, car batteries, phone chargers, radio tuning circuits and the choice of fuse ratings apply current electricity every day.
sla_exercise: State Kirchhoff's first law.::The algebraic sum of the currents at a junction is zero, because charge is conserved.||A cell of e.m.f. 12 V and internal resistance 2 Ω supplies a current of 2 A. Find the terminal p.d.::V = E - Ir = 12 - 2 x 2 = 8 V.||Calculate the r.m.s. current for an alternating current with a peak value of 5.0 A.::I_rms = 5.0/√2 = 3.5 A.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of concepts, theories and principles in Physics
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Physics
learning_activity_name: Explore the basic tenets of electromagnetism (electromagnetic force, induction and electromagnetic waves)
sla_assessment_criteria: Principles underlying the phenomenon of electromagnetism are correctly explored.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Electromagnetism links electricity and magnetism: moving charges produce magnetic fields and changing magnetic fields produce currents.
sla_notes_details: A charge q moving with velocity v in a field B experiences F = qvB sinθ, and a conductor of length L carrying current I experiences F = BIL sinθ (Fleming's left-hand rule). The field of a long straight wire is B = μ₀I/2πr and inside a solenoid B = μ₀nI. Faraday's law states that the induced e.m.f. equals the rate of change of flux linkage, ε = -N dΦ/dt, and Lenz's law says that the induced current opposes the change that produces it. Applications include generators, transformers (Vs/Vp = Ns/Np), self-inductance ε = -L dI/dt and energy in an inductor ½LI². Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerating charges, travel in vacuum at c = 3.0 x 10⁸ m/s and form a spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays, with c = fλ; they are transverse waves with E and B perpendicular.
sla_notes_illustrations: A coil of 200 turns and area 0.01 m² rotates in a field of 0.5 T; the flux linkage changes from 1.0 to 0 in 0.05 s, giving an induced e.m.f. of 200 x 5 x 10⁻³ / 0.05 = 20 V. A transformer with 100 primary and 500 secondary turns on a 24 V supply gives 120 V.
sla_notes_daily_life: Electric motors in fans and pumps, dynamos on bicycles, power transformers on the national grid, induction cookers, mobile phones and radio all rely on electromagnetism.
sla_exercise: State Lenz's law.::The direction of an induced e.m.f. or current is such that it opposes the change that produced it.||A wire of length 0.5 m carrying 4 A is at right angles to a field of 0.2 T. Find the force.::F = BIL = 0.2 x 4 x 0.5 = 0.4 N.||Find the wavelength of a radio wave of frequency 100 MHz.::λ = c/f = 3.0 x 10⁸ / 1.0 x 10⁸ = 3.0 m.

specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the concepts, theories and principles in Physics
learning_activity_name: Explore the basic tenets of electronics and telecommunication (band theory, semiconductors, transistors, logic gates and satellites)
sla_assessment_criteria: Concepts and principles related to electronics and telecommunication are correctly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Electronics uses semiconductor devices to control signals, and telecommunication uses them to send information over long distances.
sla_notes_details: Band theory explains that in conductors the valence and conduction bands overlap, in insulators there is a large energy gap and in semiconductors a small gap (about 1 eV for silicon). Doping silicon with pentavalent atoms (phosphorus) gives n-type material and with trivalent atoms (boron) gives p-type; a p-n junction forms a diode that conducts in forward bias only and is used for rectification. The transistor (npn or pnp) works as a switch or an amplifier, with Ic = βIb. An operational amplifier with negative feedback has inverting gain -Rf/Rin. Logic gates AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR process binary signals, and NAND or NOR can build any gate. In telecommunication, information is modulated (AM or FM) onto a carrier wave, transmitted through antennas, and satellites in geostationary orbit at about 36 000 km relay signals for television, phone and GPS.
sla_notes_illustrations: For an inverting op-amp with Rin = 1 kΩ and Rf = 10 kΩ the gain is -10, so an input of 0.2 V gives -2 V. A NAND gate outputs 0 only when both inputs are 1, so joining both inputs gives a NOT gate.
sla_notes_daily_life: Radios, televisions, mobile phones, calculators, security alarms, automatic doors and satellite dishes all use electronic devices and telecommunication principles.
sla_exercise: Name the type of impurity used to make p-type silicon.::A trivalent element such as boron.||Give the output of an AND gate when the inputs are 1 and 0.::0.||Why is a communications satellite placed in geostationary orbit?::It stays above the same point on the Earth (period 24 hours over the equator), so ground antennas need not track it.

sla_assessment_criteria: Concepts and principles related to atomic physics are correctly described.
sla_teaching_aids: Hydrogen spectral lamb|Diffraction grating|Prism spectrometer|Power supply|Photocell|Light source|Prism|Micro-ammeter|Voltmeter|X-ray tube|He-Ne laser|Screen|Models|Radioactive sources|GM tube|Scaler counter|Timer
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Atomic physics explains the structure of atoms and light emission, while nuclear physics explains radioactivity and energy from the nucleus.
sla_notes_details: In the Bohr model electrons occupy discrete energy levels; a transition emits or absorbs a photon of energy hf = E₂ - E₁, producing line spectra, with hydrogen levels E = -13.6/n² eV. The photoelectric effect shows light as photons: hf = φ + KEmax. de Broglie wavelength is λ = h/p. X-rays are produced when fast electrons hit a metal target, with a minimum wavelength λmin = hc/eV. LASER light is coherent and monochromatic and results from stimulated emission and population inversion. The nucleus contains protons and neutrons with mass defect Δm giving binding energy E = Δmc². Radioactive decay is random, with activity A = λN and N = N₀e^(-λt), half-life t½ = 0.693/λ. Alpha particles (helium nuclei) are stopped by paper, beta particles by aluminium and gamma rays are reduced by thick lead; fission and fusion release energy.
sla_notes_illustrations: A hydrogen electron falls from n = 3 to n = 2: E = -1.51 - (-3.40) = 1.89 eV, giving a red photon of λ = 1240/1.89 = 656 nm. A sample with half-life 8 days falls from 80 g to 10 g in 24 days.
sla_notes_daily_life: Smoke detectors, X-ray scans, barcode scanners and laser printers, cancer therapy, radiocarbon dating and nuclear power stations all use atomic and nuclear physics.
sla_exercise: State the photoelectric equation.::hf = φ + KEmax, where φ is the work function.||A radioactive source has a half-life of 6 h. What fraction remains after 18 h?::18 h is three half-lives, so (1/2)³ = 1/8 remains.||Name the three types of radiation from radioactive substances in order of increasing penetration.::Alpha, beta, gamma.

sla_method: Inquiry-based learning and Field trips and guest speakers

sla_teaching_aids: Diagram of hydroelectric power plant|Hydroelectric plant|Reference books|Solar cell testers|Wood|Solar panel|Photovoltaic (solar)|Cell|Solar cells|Model of solar panel|Wind|Feathers|Cotton wool|Wind mills|Thermometers|Wind data loggers|Flowmeters|Pressure transducers
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Energy sources supply the power for homes and industries, and physics explains how each source is converted to useful electrical energy.
sla_notes_details: Solar radiation reaches Earth at about 1 kW/m²; solar thermal collectors heat water and photovoltaic cells convert light directly to electricity with typical efficiency 15-20%. Wind energy: the power available is P = ½ρAv³, and the Betz limit means that at most 59% can be extracted. Hydropower converts gravitational potential energy to electricity, P = ηρgQh, where Q is the flow rate and h the head. Thermal reactors, either fossil-fuelled or nuclear, boil water to drive turbines; in a fission reactor control rods absorb neutrons, the moderator slows neutrons and the coolant carries away heat. Sources are compared on cost, reliability, environmental effects, renewability and efficiency, and combining them improves energy security.
sla_notes_illustrations: A wind turbine of blade radius 20 m in a 10 m/s wind of air density 1.2 kg/m³ has swept area 1257 m², so P = 0.5 x 1.2 x 1257 x 1000 = 754 kW available before losses. A hydro plant with a flow of 5 m³/s, head 40 m and efficiency 80% gives 0.8 x 1000 x 9.8 x 5 x 40 = 1.57 MW.
sla_notes_daily_life: Solar home systems, wind pumps, hydropower stations such as Julius Nyerere and Kidatu, and biomass and geothermal plants supply electricity in Tanzania and East Africa.
sla_exercise: Write the expression for the power available in wind of speed v through area A.::P = ½ρAv³.||What is the function of the moderator in a nuclear reactor?::It slows down fast neutrons so that they can cause further fission.||Give two advantages of solar energy.::It is renewable and produces no gaseous pollution during operation; it can also be used in remote areas without grid electricity.

sla_assessment_criteria: Physical concepts, theories and principles used in medical Physics are clearly explained.
sla_teaching_aids: Various models|Various diagnostic|Radiotherapy|Mammography machines|MRI machine|CT scanners|X-ray machine|Linear accelerator|Radiation detectors|Dosimeters|Ultrasound meter|Hospitals

sla_notes_intro: Medical physics applies physics to understand the human body, to diagnose diseases and to treat them.
sla_notes_details: The nervous system transmits signals as electrical impulses; a nerve cell membrane has a resting potential of about -70 mV, and an action potential of about +30 mV travels along the axon. The heart's electrical activity is recorded in an electrocardiogram (ECG) using electrodes on the skin, and abnormal waveforms show heart disorders. Diagnostic imaging includes X-rays, whose contrast depends on absorption, CT scanning that builds slices from many X-ray projections, ultrasound that uses reflection of sound of 1-15 MHz with intensity reflection coefficient depending on acoustic impedance, MRI that uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to make protons emit signals, and gamma cameras in nuclear medicine with radiotracers such as technetium-99m. Radiotherapy uses ionising radiation to destroy cancer cells, with the dose in gray (J/kg) and the equivalent dose in sieverts; safety follows time, distance and shielding.
sla_notes_illustrations: A 3.5 MHz ultrasound pulse takes 130 µs to return from an organ; with speed 1540 m/s in tissue the depth is 1540 x 130 x 10⁻⁶ / 2 = 0.10 m. A patient receives 2 Gy from radiation of weighting factor 1, so the equivalent dose is 2 Sv.
sla_notes_daily_life: Hospitals use ECG machines, ultrasound scans of pregnancy, X-rays for fractures and radiotherapy for cancer, and health workers follow radiation protection rules.
sla_exercise: What is measured by an electrocardiogram?::The electrical activity of the heart muscle as a function of time.||Why is ultrasound preferred to X-rays for scanning a foetus?::It is non-ionising and therefore safe for the developing baby, while X-rays are ionising.||State the SI unit of absorbed dose of radiation.::Gray (Gy), equal to one joule per kilogram.

sla_name: Using instruments in advanced physics experiments
sla_assessment_criteria: Various measuring instruments of current electricity, electromagnetism, electronics, telecommunication, energy sources, medicine and atomic physics are correctly used.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Advanced experiments in current electricity, electronics, atomic physics and other topics need specialised instruments used with correct technique.
sla_notes_details: In electricity, the multimeter, potentiometer, Wheatstone bridge and oscilloscope are used with proper ranges and connections. A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by a low-resistance shunt and into a voltmeter by a high-resistance multiplier. In electronics, signal generators supply input signals and the oscilloscope shows the output; transistor characteristics are plotted from readings of Ib, Ic and Vce. In atomic physics, the GM tube with a scaler measures count rates and the background count is subtracted; the spectrometer with a diffraction grating measures wavelengths using d sinθ = nλ. For the energy topic, solar cell testers and data loggers measure power output. Safety includes handling radioactive sources with tongs and keeping them shielded.
sla_notes_illustrations: To convert a galvanometer of resistance 50 Ω and full-scale current 2 mA into a 0-10 V voltmeter, a series resistor R = 10/0.002 - 50 = 4950 Ω is added. A GM tube gives 280 counts per minute with the source and 20 per minute background, so the corrected rate is 260 per minute.
sla_notes_daily_life: Electricians and biomedical technicians use meters and oscilloscopes, and radiographers monitor doses using detectors, all skills built on laboratory instrument practice.
sla_exercise: How is a galvanometer converted into an ammeter?::By connecting a low-resistance shunt in parallel with it.||Why is the background count subtracted from the count rate of a source?::Because the detector also counts radiation from the surroundings, so the corrected rate is only from the source.||What does the oscilloscope display?::The variation of voltage with time of an input signal.

sla_name: Strengths and weaknesses of instruments in advanced topics
sla_assessment_criteria: The strengths and weaknesses of various measuring instruments and techniques used in Physics are appropriately analysed.
sla_teaching_aids: Various measuring instruments|Journal papers|Research articles|Online resources
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Comparing the instruments and techniques used in advanced physics helps to select those with suitable accuracy, range and safety.
sla_notes_details: The potentiometer draws no current at balance so it measures e.m.f. more accurately than a voltmeter, but it is slower to use. The Wheatstone bridge is very accurate for resistance near the balance point but is affected by heating and contact resistance. Digital multimeters are convenient and have high input resistance, while analogue meters give parallax error. The oscilloscope is good for fast signals, but reading accuracy is limited. The GM tube is easy to use for counting but cannot distinguish the type of radiation or its energy, and it has a dead time, whereas a scintillation counter gives energy information at higher cost. Techniques such as the diffraction grating method measure wavelengths more precisely than a prism, because dispersion is linear and larger. Analysis considers cost, safety, calibration and skill required.
sla_notes_illustrations: To find the e.m.f. of a cell, a voltmeter of finite resistance reads slightly less than E because a small current flows through r, whereas the potentiometer at balance gives E itself; the potentiometer is therefore chosen for precision work.
sla_notes_daily_life: Choosing digital rather than analogue meters, or a shielded probe rather than an open source, illustrates how technicians compare tools for safety and accuracy.
sla_exercise: Why does a potentiometer measure e.m.f. more accurately than a voltmeter?::At balance it draws no current from the cell, so there is no voltage drop across the internal resistance.||State one limitation of a GM tube.::It cannot identify the energy or type of radiation and it has dead time after each count.||Why do digital meters reduce reading errors?::They display the value directly, removing parallax and interpolation errors of scale readings.

main_competence_name: Conduct experiments in Physics
specific_competence_name: Carry out experiments in Physics
learning_activity_name: Design and carry out scientific experiments related to current electricity, electromagnetism, electronics, telecommunication, energy sources, medical physics and atomic physics
sla_assessment_criteria: Experiments related to current electricity, electromagnetism, electronics, telecommunication, energy sources, medical Physics and atomic physics are correctly designed and carried out.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Advanced experiments apply the scientific method to investigate laws in electricity, electromagnetism, electronics, atomic physics, energy and medical physics.
sla_notes_details: Each experiment states an aim, hypothesis, variables, apparatus, procedure, safety, data tables and analysis. Examples are the internal resistance of a cell by plotting V against I (gradient -r, intercept E), the variation of resistance of a thermistor with temperature, the characteristics of a diode, the charging and discharging of a capacitor, verification of the inverse square law for gamma radiation, the wavelength of laser light using a grating, the efficiency of a solar panel at different angles, and the magnetic field of a solenoid using a Hall probe. Graphs are linearised, for example ln(A) against t for radioactive decay with gradient -λ, and results are evaluated with uncertainties and improvements suggested. Virtual laboratories may be used where equipment is limited.
sla_notes_illustrations: Data for a cell: V = 1.45, 1.40, 1.35, 1.30 V for I = 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40 A. The gradient is -0.5 V/A so r = 0.5 Ω, and the intercept 1.50 V is E.
sla_notes_daily_life: Testing the quality of batteries in a shop, checking sunlight for a solar panel installation or verifying safe distances from a source involve the same experimental methods.
sla_exercise: What quantities are obtained from a graph of terminal p.d. against current for a cell?::The e.m.f. from the intercept on the V axis and the internal resistance from the negative of the gradient.||What should be plotted to find the decay constant of a radioisotope?::ln(activity) against time; the gradient is -λ.||State one safety precaution when using a laser.::Never look directly into the beam or its reflections; use low power and avoid pointing it at people.

specific_competence_name: Conduct a project in Physics

sla_name: Completing and submitting the physics project report
sla_assessment_criteria: Projects have been completed and report submitted.
sla_references: TET(2023), PHYSICS SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The research project started in Form Five ends with improving the prototype or refining the data, and submitting a full scientific report.
sla_notes_details: Students appraise their prototypes or findings, test them again, correct weaknesses and record the improved results. The report contains a title page, acknowledgement, abstract, table of contents, introduction with background and objectives, literature review, methodology, results and analysis using tables and graphs with uncertainties, discussion, conclusion and recommendations, references and appendices. Work should be original, data must be honestly reported, and sources properly cited. The report is assessed on the design, the scientific process, presentation and the clarity of communication, and results may be displayed at a science fair or exhibition.
sla_notes_illustrations: A group that built a solar dryer improves it by adding a black absorber plate and re-tests: drying time of tomatoes falls from 3 days in the open to 1.5 days, and the report presents temperature graphs, cost and recommendations for farmers.
sla_notes_daily_life: Completed projects such as solar dryers, water filters or small wind turbines can be adapted by communities and small businesses, and the report-writing skills are useful in any career.
sla_exercise: List three sections that must appear in a project report.::Abstract, methodology and results (also conclusion and references).||Why should recommendations follow the conclusion in a project report?::They suggest how the findings can be used or how the study can be improved or extended.||What is the purpose of testing and improving a prototype?::To find weaknesses and refine the design so that it solves the identified problem better.
